input.brief: Full-stack developer: business software by day, open source libraries (NestJS, Italian e-health FSE, AI agents) and a console-style game launcher by night

direction.name: The contact sheet
direction.idea: Show everything at once, small, in order. The work is laid out like a photographer's contact sheet or an archive drawer: dozens of small frames in strict rows, with all text set at one small size. Nothing is featured, which is the point: the volume and consistency of the body of work is the statement, and the visitor does the choosing. It suits people and studios whose strength is range and output.
direction.composition: The name, or one sentence about the work, sits at display size (6–9vw) across the top of the first screen, and the sheet begins directly under it, still inside the first screen. The first screen opens with three or four short blocks of small text across the top on a 12-column grid (who, what, where to reach them), all at 14–16px, and immediately below, the sheet begins: rows of thumbnails at a fixed height (90–140px) with their natural widths, 6–10px gaps, each project forming a run of four to eight frames preceded by its title in the same small text. The sheet fills the whole page width edge to edge with 16–20px margins. Hovering a run dims the others and shows that project's one-line description in a fixed position. A single enlarged frame may interrupt the sheet once per screen at four times the size.
direction.typography: One face. The name at display size on the first screen; everything else at one text size and one small size; hierarchy below the name comes from position and from a single brighter ink for titles.
direction.colour: Black or white ground, so the thumbnails are the only colour.
direction.imagery: Many images: at least 24 frames to make a sheet. They can be project photographs from the dealt set cropped to mixed ratios, or page captures of the work. Square corners, no captions on the frames.
direction.richness: Density and order. The mass of small images forms a texture; the strict rows keep it calm.
direction.pitfalls: With fewer than about 20 images it looks unfinished; choose another direction. Do not add a big headline above the sheet. On a phone the frames become two per row at a fixed height and each run scrolls sideways. Rows that run past the right edge read as clipped in screenshots and to most visitors: wrap the frames onto the next line, or end each row inside the grid.

hero.name: Lit strip, four corners
hero.blueprint: One near-black field with a single lit band. Four small pieces of text at 14px, medium weight, sit in the corners on 72px side margins and 44px top and bottom margins: the name top-left, one link top-right, one sentence saying what this is bottom-left (max 36ch), the single action as a text link bottom-right. Across the vertical middle runs one horizontal strip of photographs, 34vh tall (about 300px), each at its natural width with 10px gaps and square corners: eleven or more frames in a flex row wider than the viewport, so the first and last visible frames are cropped by the left and right edges. The frame nearest the centre is at full brightness; the others sit at filter: brightness(0.55) and brighten on hover or as they reach the centre. Under the centred frame, aligned to its left edge, its title is set in the same 14px text. The top quarter and the bottom quarter of the screen stay empty and dark. The strip scrolls sideways with overflow-x: auto and scroll-snap; never hijack vertical scroll.
hero.mobile: The strip stays a single sideways-scrolling row but grows to 46vh tall, so one frame and the cropped edges of its neighbours fill the width. The name and the link sit at the top on 20px margins; the sentence and the action stack bottom-left under the strip at 14px. Dark space remains above and below the strip, about 12% of the height each.
hero.headline: None at display size: the name at 14px in a corner and one sentence of up to 60 characters.

motion.name: Drag row
motion.description: A row of large items wider than the screen that the visitor pulls sideways: native horizontal scrolling with scroll snapping, the first item aligned to the page margin and the last allowed to run off the edge so the row visibly continues. No carousel library, no arrows, no dots.

sections.name: One strip per project
sections.blueprint: The left 13% of the width is a `position: sticky` column holding the section name at 28px and, beneath it, two text filters at 15px, the active one in full ink. To its right each project is one horizontal strip of four to six images, all exactly 190px tall at their natural widths (`height: 190px; width: auto`), 8px apart, the last one cut off by the right viewport edge with `overflow: hidden`. Under each strip, one line at 13px spread across the strip's width: project name flush left, a three-word descriptor at the centre, the year flush right. 45px separate one strip from the next, so four projects fit on a 900px screen and ten make a page. Square corners; no captions on individual frames. Hovering a strip dims the other strips to 40% opacity. There is no heading beyond the section name in the rail.
sections.mobile: The rail becomes a single line above the list: section name left, filters right. Strips are 120px tall and each scrolls sideways on its own with `overflow-x: auto` and scroll snapping. The caption line keeps the name left and the year right; the descriptor is dropped.

sections.name: Side facts, wide paragraph
sections.blueprint: Two rows share one vertical line at 34% of the viewport width. Row one: in a 160px column at the left margin, three label and value pairs stack with 20px between them, each a label in the soft ink with its value beneath in full ink, all at 13px (founded, based in, team size). From the 34% line a five-line paragraph at clamp(20px, 1.7vw, 26px), leading 1.35, runs to 90% of the width. Row two starts 120px lower and repeats the logic for the record of the practice: one plain word at 13px at the far left (awards, press, clients), then from the 34% line two list columns, each 260px wide with a 64px gutter, at 13px with 10px between lines: name at the left, year at the right in the soft ink. No heading; the paragraph opens the section. Each list comfortably holds 6–12 lines. No photographs are needed.
sections.mobile: Everything aligns to the left margin. The paragraph comes first at 19px. The three label and value pairs follow as a two-column grid at 14px. The two record lists stack with 40px between them, each opened by its plain word in full ink.

sections.name: Photo strip, three-cell bar
sections.blueprint: A saturated flat field about 80svh tall. Across the top, 48px from the section edge, a strip of small photographs runs off both sides: all 150px tall at differing widths (3:4, 1:1, 3:2 in turn), 8px gaps, ten or more, drifting slowly as a marquee. A heading of two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px) sits 72px below the strip at the left margin. 40px below the heading, the newsletter or booking form is one bar spanning the content width, 96px tall, divided into three equal cells with 8px gaps. Each cell is a filled block in a tone one step from the field with one radius: the first two are inputs (name, email) with placeholder text centred at 18px, the third is the submit action in the inverse colours with its word centred. Focus changes a cell's fill to the lightest tone. Small print at 13px sits under the first and third cells.
sections.mobile: The strip is 110px tall and scrolls by touch. The heading follows at 9vw. The three cells stack as full-width filled blocks 60px tall with 8px gaps, the submit block last. Small print sits beneath the stack, left-aligned.

sections.name: A footer of tiles
sections.blueprint: The footer is the last two rows of a board: filled tiles with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, every cell used. Upper row, each tile 220px tall: a statement tile in columns 1–4 with one sentence at 24px top-left and the legal text at 12px bottom-left; a navigation tile in columns 5–7 with a plain list at 16px; a tile in columns 8–9 giving the city and local time as text; an email tile in columns 10–12 with the address at 20px as a link, bottom-left. Lower row, 320px tall: a tile in the ink colour spanning columns 1–8 with the wordmark set large (about 9vw) and centred, and a tile in the accent colour in columns 9–12 with a two-to-four-word invitation top-left at 28px and an arrow, drawn as inline SVG with 4px strokes, in its bottom-right corner; the whole accent tile is a link.
sections.mobile: Two columns of tiles with 6px gaps: the wordmark tile full width first at 160px tall, the accent tile full width next, then navigation and email side by side, then time and statement. Every tile keeps 20px padding and top-left text.

references.name: Gil Huybrecht
references.idea: A portfolio as a contact sheet: every project is a numbered run of miniature page screenshots on black, and all text is set at one small size.
references.hero: Black field on a seven-column grid with 14px margins. The top band is plain white text at one size, about 16px: name in column one, availability in column two, a services list from column three, a longer awards list from column five, then 'Profile' and 'Email me' at the right. List items are indented one step under their label. Below the lists roughly 300px of black is left empty. At mid-height the thumbnail grid begins: one small website screenshot per column, about 190px wide, each topped by a number at its right corner, with the project name over the first of each run. Two tiny toggle chips sit in the bottom corners.
references.type: One neo-grotesk at a single size, about 16px (1.1vw), medium-bold with tight tracking, white on black, for everything: name, lists, labels, numbers, footer. There is no headline; hierarchy comes only from column position and indentation.
references.colour: #000000 #fcfcfc #272727 #8a8a8a — Pure black with white text; the only colour is whatever appears inside the screenshot thumbnails. Inactive toggle words drop to mid-grey on a dark grey chip.
references.imagery: Miniature full-page captures of the designer's client sites, uncropped at natural aspect ratios, square corners, no frames or shadows, about 190px wide, sitting directly on black.
references.layout: Seven equal columns with 14px gutters and margins for the whole page. Thumbnails align to columns but not to rows: each hangs from its own label at its own height, so bottoms are ragged. Projects flow continuously and wrap across rows.

sections.description: A seven-column field of screenshot thumbnails on black. Each project is a consecutive run of four to six thumbnails; the project name sits above the first, and every thumbnail carries its sequence number right-aligned above it in the same 16px white. Thumbnails keep their real proportions, so a row mixes 100px-tall and 280px-tall items with ragged bottoms and about 90px of black between rows. Runs break mid-row and continue on the next line with no divider.

View toggles. Two fixed chip pairs sit in the viewport's bottom corners: the left switches between a grid and a gallery view, the right between a normal and a novelty perspective mode. Each pair is a small dark-grey rounded rectangle containing two words, the active one white and the inactive grey, at the same 16px as all other text.

After about a screen of empty black, one band of text on the same seven columns: year and privacy link stacked at the left, then two columns of stacked social links, then two single links toward the right edge. Same size and weight as the header, no rule, no logo.

steal: Set every piece of text on the page at one size and weight and build hierarchy only from column position and a one-step indent under labels.
Show projects as numbered runs of uncropped page screenshots at natural heights on a strict column grid, leaving the bottoms ragged.
Leave a deliberate 300px void between the text header and the first row of work so the lists read as a letterhead.
references.media: A contact-sheet wall: one fixed WebGL canvas draws about 84 full-page screenshots of client sites at a single 190px width and their native ratios, every page of each project in reading order. Once scrolled, every screen is about three rows, roughly 48% picture and 52% black, with text under 1% and the labels above each frame, never on it; there is no video.
references.motion: The preloader counts at about 13% a second for some 7-8s while the screenshot textures load, although the document loaded in 1.66s; then the first-row thumbnails rise into their slots in random order and a dark veil lifts. Lenis over a 4440px scroll proxy redraws the fixed wall with no pins or reveals; panel and hover moves use transform .75s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1), and pictures fade over 1s ease-out on the phone.

references.name: PROOOOF
references.idea: The product's output is the page: a wall of photos each wearing its coloured EXIF strip, with all the copy folded into one small floating card.
references.hero: The whole viewport is a six-column masonry of photographs on a warm off-white ground with about 15px gutters, columns offset vertically so rows never line up. Each photo has a flat strip fused to its bottom edge carrying tiny monospaced capture data, every strip a different solid colour (black, red, orange, yellow, violet, green). Dead centre floats a white card about 380px wide and 410px tall with roughly 28px corner radius and a soft shadow. It contains an extended wordmark with chained O's, a two-row accordion with the first row open, an App Store badge and a monospaced line of links. There is no navigation.
references.type: An extended, heavy wordmark with interlocked O's is the only display type. Card text is Wintyr VF at about 14-16px, medium weight for accordion headings. EXIF strips and footer links are monospace at roughly 8-13px. No headline anywhere.
references.colour: #f3eee9 #fafafa #191818 #ff6a2b #f7c531 #5a4fcf — Colour comes from the photographs and the saturated caption strips, one hue per photo. Card and gutters stay off-white; a final panel flips to near-black with grey characters.
references.imagery: Casual travel, food, pet and concert photos in mixed portrait and landscape crops, square corners, ungraded, tiled edge to edge. The page ends on an ASCII-art rendering of a hand holding a camera.
references.layout: Effectively a single screen: the photo wall sits behind a centred card that carries every word. Six columns on desktop, two on mobile where the card widens to nearly full width. The only second scene is a dark, inset ASCII panel.

sections.description: All product copy lives in the centred card as an accordion: a row with heading left and chevron right, a hairline divider, the open panel's four-line paragraph, a centred store badge, another divider, a collapsed second row, then a small monospaced line with a version number and underlined links. The card stays put while the wall remains visible on all four sides.

Each tile is a photo with a data strip attached below: two or three rows of monospaced text, four values spread evenly across the first row, date and time at opposite ends of the second, maker and model on the third. Strip and text colours change per tile, for example yellow on black, black on yellow, white on violet, so a uniform grid looks varied.

The closing panel is a near-black rectangle inset with wide margins and filled edge to edge with rows of grey ASCII characters that resolve into a picture of a hand gripping a camera. One line of tiny monospaced uppercase text sits at the exact centre as the call to action. No button and no logo.

steal: Show the product's output at wall scale as the background and confine all copy to one small card on top of it.
Give every repeated tile its own flat accent colour for the caption strip so a strict grid reads as lively.
Hold the explanatory copy in an accordion inside the hero card so the page needs no scrolling.

references.name: davesocozy
references.idea: A collage artist introduces himself by building a collage: each scroll step changes one caption and drops more paper cut-outs onto a green cutting mat.
references.hero: Cream page with a single centred object: a green cutting mat 776px wide by 582px tall (54% of viewport width), printed with a white grid, an inner border and diagonal guide lines, casting a soft shadow. One small portrait photo lies at its exact centre, tilted about three degrees. A one-line greeting in bold monospace at 32px sits 30px above the mat. The four viewport corners hold fixed controls: a glossy green flower logo top-left and three dark brown bevelled buttons in uppercase mono (shop top-right, Instagram bottom-left, enter studio bottom-right). A small scroll cue sits under the mat.
references.type: Martian Mono everywhere. Bold 32px for the changing caption (one or two centred lines); 12px tracked uppercase for buttons and hints. Only two sizes, and the mono face gives a label-maker feel that suits a workbench.
references.colour: #ede6d4 #5c894e #241a15 #3d2b22 #ffffff — Warm cream ground, mat green as the one large colour block, chocolate brown for text and buttons. Other colour arrives only through the collage scraps.
references.imagery: Cut-out vintage imagery (twin-lens camera, game console, microphone, globe, fox, fish, crumpled paper) and one portrait photo, each rotated a few degrees with a slight shadow, scattered on the mat like paper scraps. A 3D room follows.
references.layout: A single fixed stage: nothing scrolls away, the mat stays centred while its contents and the caption above change. Corner-pinned buttons replace a nav bar. Empty cream margins of about 23% of the width on each side.

sections.description: Scroll-driven introduction on the pinned stage. The caption above the mat is replaced sentence by sentence, each as two centred lines of bold mono, and with every sentence two or three more cut-outs land on the mat around the portrait at loose angles, some overlapping it and a few flying in from outside. By the last caption the mat holds about ten scraps and a line of tiny uppercase instructions appears beneath the caption.

After the intro the mat hands over to a canvas-rendered studio room that the visitor looks around with the mouse and clicks into (the page's own text lists a desk of collages, a wall of framed pieces and a television). The four corner buttons persist as the only chrome. The room itself is not in the captured frames, so its composition is unknown.

steal: Pin one physical work surface in the centre and let scrolling add objects to it while a single caption line above changes, instead of stacking sections.
Put navigation in the four viewport corners as small tactile buttons so the centre stays free.
Rotate every cut-out by a different few degrees and give each a small shadow so flat images read as paper.
